details:
In recent years, VRChat's performance ranking system has barely been functioning.

This is because there are no penalties for being rated "Very Poor," leading to calls for the limits to be raised.

(This post does not aim to debate the specific numerical thresholds for performance ranks, so I will not discuss those figures here.)

Now is the time to reinstate polygon upload limits to prevent users from becoming complacent.

Admittedly, polygon count has a smaller impact on performance compared to other factors like material slots or texture sizes.

However,

Users who do not care about polygon count—the most easily understood metric—often show a similarly low level of awareness regarding the optimization of textures, materials, and PhysBones.

We should bring back limits not merely to restrict the polygon count itself, but to enforce the stance that "if you cannot manage even this simple metric, you are not qualified to upload content."

That said, the root cause often lies not with the users uploading the avatars, but with the artists creating the outfits and items installed on them.

These creators tend to prioritize the visual aesthetic they desire while disregarding machine resource constraints.

Therefore, I believe we should test the waters with a limit of 500,000 polygons, or perhaps a slightly more lenient 1 million.

This is similar to the existing 500MB limit on texture memory.

(Personally, I think around 300,000 polygons would suffice, but since some players might dislike that, we would need to carefully monitor their reactions.)
title: Time to bring back the polygon count upload limit.
